interpretation: Measurement design, not estimator sophistication, sets what is recoverable: identifiability is a rank property of the Poisson-weighted Jacobian (F-001). This is direct evidence for H2 (Q-003) in the idealised regime. Two error classes behave differently: basis misspecification is systematic and dose-independent (F-003), whereas spectral mismatch at these magnitudes is design-dependent and can hide below the noise floor (F-004). A learned method cannot repair a rank-deficient design; comparisons of learned methods must therefore be made within an identifiable design or they measure the prior, not the physics.
limitations: Idealised 2D toy: 48x48 pixels, parallel beam, additive mixtures with no volume conservation, Poisson-only noise, no scatter/detector blur/pile-up/beam hardening correction. Statistics on a ray subset, not the full image. Shared forward model for data and estimator (no inverse crime avoidance): this is a best case and overstates achievable accuracy. D-002: iodine K-edge under-resolved on the 1 keV table, so NO absolute iodine-concentration claim is made. Elemental reference densities, not tissue mixtures. CPU/MPS laptop only; nothing here validates GPU or HPC. Absolute spectrum normalisation UNVERIFIED (designs compared at equal photons per ray by construction).
next_experiment: EXP-003: spectral-mismatch power study. Sweep perturbation magnitude (tilt 0 to 30%, energy scale 0 to 5%) at fixed design, with realisation count chosen from a pre-computed power analysis so the detection floor is known BEFORE running, and an analytic bias prediction from first-order perturbation of the MLE to compare against. This resolves F-004 and is the prerequisite for any inverse-crime-free comparison under H1.
unresolved: Whether dual-kVp is genuinely insensitive to smooth spectral error or (f) was merely under-powered. Whether the K-edge-resolved table (T-006) changes iodine conditioning. How conclusions move under a mismatched forward model (the inverse-crime-free setting of H1/Q-002).
what_failed: Prediction (f) partially falsified (F-004): dual-kVp cells on the 2-material phantom showed mismatch bias only 0.73-1.77x their noise floor, i.e. not detectably biased, while photon-counting designs showed 6-8x. The pre-registered criterion assumed all mismatch produces detectable bias; at the chosen perturbation sizes and 20 realisations it is under-powered for dual-kVp. Under-power vs genuine insensitivity is NOT resolved by this experiment.

interpretation: The durable scientific content is narrower than first stated. Measurement design sets what is recoverable, but the headline rank results are arithmetic, not evidence; the empirical content is the conditioning and noise comparison among IDENTIFIABLE designs (F-007), where photon counting is better than dual-kVp at equal basis size and equal photons. Spectral mismatch always biases a nominal-spectrum estimator (F-005); whether that bias is visible depends on the material scored, the dose and the statistic, which is a warning about evaluation design for H1/Q-002. Basis misspecification remains systematic and dose-independent (F-008). This episode is itself evidence that pre-registered criteria need a power analysis and an all-material scope before they are binding.
limitations: All prior limitations stand (idealised 2D toy, shared forward model for data and estimator, ray-subset statistics, D-002 iodine K-edge under-resolved, laptop CPU/MPS only, absolute spectrum normalisation unverified). Added: the emp/CRLB check cannot detect a wrong attenuation table or spectrum; equal-photon comparison excludes pure gain mismatch by construction; the energy-integrating Poisson model (noise applied to E-weighted counts) is idealised; headline recovery numbers (iodine RMSE 0.005 g/cm3 vs a 0.005 g/cm3 insert; calcium 0.085 vs 0.1-0.3) are NOT evidence of good recovery.
next_experiment: EXP-003 (revised by this review): spectral-mismatch bias study driven by DETERMINISTIC noise-free bias as the primary quantity, with Monte-Carlo only to establish detectability. Required design changes: score ALL materials, not iodine alone; pre-compute the detection floor and choose the realisation count from a power analysis BEFORE running; separate gain mismatch from shape mismatch; and compare against a first-order analytic bias prediction. Prerequisite for any inverse-crime-free comparison under H1.
unresolved: Whether photon counting retains its advantage once detector response, charge sharing and pile-up are modelled (all absent here). How conclusions move under a genuinely mismatched forward model (H1/Q-002). Whether the K-edge-resolved table (T-006) changes iodine conditioning.
what_failed: Three overstatements in my own original findings, all corrected: (1) F-001 presented rank results as empirical when rank<=min(n_meas,k) is forced by matrix shape, and quoted a 2.70x noise penalty for photon counting that confounded design with basis size - at equal basis size photon counting is 2.5x BETTER. (2) F-002 called an emp/CRLB agreement 'validation of the forward model' when it is a self-consistency check that a wrong table or spectrum would pass equally; the quoted 11% was actually 12.5%. (3) F-004 claimed dual-kVp was 'not detectably biased' under mismatch; a noise-free calculation shows bias is ALWAYS present, and the dual-kVp energy-scale case is clearly biased (4x floor). The pre-registered criterion was defective in two ways: iodine-only scoring, and requiring significance at both dose levels so the noisier level dominated. A unit mislabel (g/cm3 vs g/cm2) in the run metrics was also corrected.

what_worked: Rank/identifiability verdicts are robust to the rank threshold over 1e-2..1e-10. Conditioning numbers and the misspecification result survived review. The mismatch implementation was audited and contains NO cancellation bug: the tilt is a shape change with mean-weighted factor ~1, so rescaling to equal photons removes only overall gain (a pure gain mismatch is excluded by design, which is a scope limit, not an error).

interpretation: The headline ranking is an artifact of the metric, not of method quality: simplex 'wins' by clipping unphysical boundary values, while sum_to_one - which solves the physics exactly where the model holds - comes last. Reporting s1 alone on a two-regime phantom would rank a clipped estimator above an exact one (F-016). This is a benchmark-design result that applies to the real AAPM data too, where boundary pixels are ~5% of the image.
limitations: SYNTHETIC DATA ONLY - no AAPM case data was processed, so no AAPM-dependent or leaderboard-comparable number exists. 32x32 vs the real 512x512; the official s1 divides by 3*512^2 so the magnitudes are not comparable. Image-domain only (no fan-beam projector, so the transmission-domain methods the winners used are untested). TV lam=1e-4 was picked by a coarse scan on the same synthetic problem, so its 36% gain is optimistic. AIR_CUTOFF_PER_CM=0.1 is a modelling choice untested on real data. No U-Net yet (T-012).

interpretation: The headline claim is supported: a label-free consistency objective fits the measurements BETTER than methods that get the physics right, while being far more wrong about materials - low forward residual is not evidence of material accuracy. But the prior-ablation half of this experiment is inconclusive by my own design error, and the P2 inversion is unexplained. Scope: synthetic procedural phantoms, image domain, 32x32 - NOT AAPM data and NOT the projection domain the published winners used.
limitations: Synthetic data only; image domain only (no fan-beam projector exists, so no sinogram-domain conclusion is available); 13 val cases; 3 seeds; prior_weight fixed at 1.0 and never tuned; B2 early-stops on validation LABELS (disclosed); test split never loaded. Critically, the image-domain linear model these rungs assume is wrong by 6-8% on REAL AAPM images (F-025), so none of these numbers should be expected to transfer.
next_experiment: Do NOT rerun this ladder. The binding gap is the forward model: image-domain linear inversion is 6-8% wrong on real AAPM data, so the next experiment must be a fan-beam projector + projection-domain consistency, which is also the regime the published winners used.

what_failed: P2 FAIL: B3's material error was NOT seed-unstable (cv 0.035, predicted >0.2) while its CONSISTENCY loss was (cv 0.61, predicted <0.05) - the exact opposite of my prediction, and I have no explanation yet; it suggests the implicit prior selects a consistent member of the ambiguous family rather than a random one. P3 FAIL and P5 FAIL are design errors of mine, not results (F-023): P3 tested a unit-weight SOFT penalty against the >5x effect F-019 proved for a HARD constraint, and I set no weight in the pre-registration. what_worked: P1 confirmed emphatically and is the main result: B3 attains the LOWEST consistency loss of all ten rungs (9.6e-5, 5x better than classical B0's 4.7e-4) while its tissue RMSE is 26x worse than B0 and 8.7x worse than supervised B2, with null|cos| 0.993. A capacity control (F-022) rules out undertraining: supervised saturates at 0.037 after 19x epochs and 4x capacity, so the network floor is only 7.8% of B3's error and the identifiability gap is 92%.

interpretation: NUMERICAL, preliminary, scope: 20 train cases, noise-free, zero-thickness exact null vector, uniform/smooth/random swap fields as stand-ins for real error patterns. (1) Gate as pre-registered: PASS for calc_l0 (both residual levels), calc_l1 (classical level only), bimodal, w1_marginal (flagged weak supervision); FAIL for tv_a. Caveat: P1 and bimodal have their minimum at the truth by construction (truth calcification ~0, truth composition near-vertex), and for all four label-free priors the wrong-label margin is carried entirely by the data term. (2) Main new fact: the visibility of an adipose<->fibro error depends strongly on its spatial structure. A uniform swap is seen at |t|=0.01-0.08, but spatially varying swaps are 6-14x weaker in RMSE (smooth) and ~15-60x weaker (rough) than the uniform one per unit t, and a rough swap of |t|<=1.1 stays BELOW the 1e-6 MSE that physics-only networks reach (smooth: below up to 0.47). This explains how networks reach projection RMSE ~1e-3 with large pattern errors (the puzzle left open by F-041): high-frequency A/F errors average out along rays. Resolving them label-free needs a solver residual MSE of ~1e-8-1e-9 (classical level), not a network-level fit; at the classical level (2e-8) a rough swap is resolved only for |t|>=0.16. (3) Calcification absence / sum knowledge act on the n direction only (calc priors have zero effect on swaps), and trained networks already satisfy them approximately (calcification <=1.8e-3, |S-1|~0.03-0.08), so these priors do not address the dominant network failure mode (spatially varying A/F error). This weakens hypothesis H1/H2 as the explanation of the network failures; it does not weaken the per-ray identifiability (F-043).
limitations: Profiles are around the truth (local, assume convergence to the truth basin); swap fields are synthetic stand-ins; 20 train cases; mean-over-rays MSE; the lambda windows used train labels (so not label-free in their selection); P1/bimodal pass by construction; TV and w1 use clipped a; projection MSE metric is the training loss scale but a ray-weighted or log loss would rescale the floors.
